questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It being outside of Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was way easier than I thought it would be

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some, but I didn't need that much

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different ones. But they put all exchange students in houses on campus where we stayed 3 or 4 per house, and had our own kitchen and bathroom and everything. This was in West Residence which I would really recommend, as it is also close to all the shops.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans are very good, Guelph has won a price for best meal plans in Canada or something. You don't need to buy one before you get there, as you can just see as you go along. When I got there I bought the 'ultra meal plan' where you pay 300 CAD and then when you run out you can just top up any amount you want. Going with the meal plan just gives you a 10% discount on the food and you can still pay 'full price' just with your credit card

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The kitchens are empty and they don't include any bedding. Other than that it is very easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky though, that my exams and classes all fit together. I had friends over there that struggled quite a lot with that.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was just by emailing them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it on time and you should be fine

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was below University of Copenhagen but not as much as I thought, which was good

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The way of grading was different, but that's just the whole american school system in general

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Urban Economics", "International Finance", "The Strategy of M&A" and "Money, Credit and Finance"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were good

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lots of sport to watch and do. For instance, I played a lot of squash which I had never played before going there

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: See as much sports as possible, especially on the uni since it's free for students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go traveling all you can, to the US, to Toronto, to the west side of Canada like British Columbia to see the mountains. There is plenty to do!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I was a bit older than the friend group I ended up in but everything was very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with exchange students. Best tip is to be very present the first two weeks of introduction as this is where you'll meet all your friends for the semester

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets are very different in quality to Copenhagen but other than that none was too challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Make sure you get accomodation on campus, my application deadline was 3rd of June before my fall semester. 2. Don't seek to spend time with Danes but get out of your comfort zone at the START introduction as everyone is so nice and there is so much to do. 3. GO CANOOING by the boathouse before it gets too cold!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, who I'll be staying friends with for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying afloat with money

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
